claims.claim: The dataset contains exactly 2,811,774 rows and 7 columns in twcs.csv (516,508,641 bytes).
claims.evidence: Direct CSV file stream count and SHA-256 computation (cd297fcfa1bf6f99938be242e8e578980bc6d1b96adc8691abec9a39175b03c0).
claims.potential_problem: None. Fully verified against raw bytes.

claims.claim: All 2,811,774 tweet_id values are unique, non-null, and integer parseable.
claims.evidence: COUNT(DISTINCT tweet_id) = 2,811,774; zero duplicate or malformed IDs.

claims.claim: Timestamps span from 2008-05-08 to 2017-12-03 with 100% parse success.
claims.evidence: datetime.strptime parser succeeded on all 2,811,774 rows with format '%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %z %Y'.
claims.potential_problem: Data is heavily non-uniform across the span (>85% in 2016-2017).
claims.required_correction: Document temporal non-uniformity alongside the date bounds.

claims.evidence: Parent created strictly before child: 2,013,521 links (99.997%); Timestamp ties: 56 links (0.003%); Temporal inversions: 0 links (0.000%).
claims.potential_problem: Describing as '100% strictly chronological' ignores the 56 timestamp ties.
claims.required_correction: Correct prose to state '99.997% strictly chronological with 56 (0.003%) timestamp ties and 0 temporal inversions'.

claims.claim: 2,013,577 (99.81%) of parent pointers resolve within the dataset; 3,862 (0.19%) are dangling clipped roots.
claims.evidence: SQL join between child in_response_to_tweet_id and parent tweet_id.
claims.potential_problem: Dangling pointers must not cause crashes during conversation reconstruction.
claims.required_correction: Document handling of clipped conversation roots as independent trees.

claims.claim: Exactly 108 support accounts exist in the dataset, accounting for all 1,273,931 outbound tweets.
claims.evidence: SELECT author_id, COUNT(*) WHERE inbound = 0 GROUP BY author_id yields exactly 108 non-numeric brand handles.

claims.claim: All 188,447 (9.36%) Inbound -> Inbound links represent multipart customer messages.
claims.evidence: Deep-dive analysis revealed only 85,419 (45.33%) are Same-Author, while 103,028 (54.67%) are Different-Author customer interactions. Among same-author, only ~35.4k occur within 120s.
claims.potential_problem: Treating all Inbound->Inbound as multipart caused false grouping of third-party comments and delayed customer self-replies.
claims.required_correction: Reclassify: 54.67% are third-party customer comments; only same-author rapid successions (<=120s) should be candidate multipart messages.

claims.claim: 120 seconds is the definitive threshold for grouping multipart customer tweets.
claims.evidence: Empirical threshold evaluation: <=30s captures 8.2%, <=60s captures 23.0%, <=120s captures 41.5%, <=180s captures 50.4% of same-author chains.
claims.potential_problem: A pure time-delta rule without textual continuity (e.g. sentence completion, 1/2 numbering) risks false grouping.
claims.required_correction: Retain 120s as a preliminary working heuristic, but flag as an Open Question for Phase 2 to combine time-delta with linguistic continuity signals.

claims.claim: AppleSupport has 106,646 usable customer->support interaction pairs and 76,365 unique customers.
claims.evidence: Direct SQL join on inbound parent to AppleSupport outbound child across the indexed dataset.
Normalized string hashing (lowercase, stripped punctuation, mentions, URLs) on 106,646 customer query texts.
claims.potential_problem: Normalized string duplication is not identical to semantic near-duplication (different phrasings of the same question).
claims.required_correction: Explicitly clarify that 2.73% measures lexical normalized duplication, not semantic intent duplication.

claims.claim: 52.58% DM redirection in AppleSupport represents an Information-Gathering & Escalation Action.
claims.evidence: AppleSupport tweets requesting DM consistently ask for device serial numbers, IMEI, or Apple ID credentials after initial triage.
claims.confidence: HIGH (as historical behavior), MEDIUM (as operational ground truth)
claims.potential_problem: Historical DM redirection does not automatically mean automation could never resolve the issue if private APIs existed.
claims.required_correction: Distinguish historical private-channel deflection behavior from future operational escalation ground truth.

claims.claim: The future AI Support Agent will be grounded primarily in historical AppleSupport interactions, not modern external documentation.
claims.evidence: Task specification requires learning how the brand historically resolved issues from twcs.csv.
claims.potential_problem: Silently mixing modern support.apple.com articles into historical 2017 evaluation would contaminate the benchmark.
claims.required_correction: Explicitly lock historical interactions as primary evidence; modern external docs are strictly out-of-scope for primary benchmark.

claims.claim: For turn k, the model receives (C1, S1, ..., Ck) and must not see Sk or future turns.
claims.required_correction: None. Keep as verified design principle.

claims.claim: A chronological time-based split is mandatory to prevent lookahead leakage.
claims.evidence: Temporal clustering shows iOS 11 rollout occurred in Oct-Nov 2017; random split would leak future software release knowledge into earlier training data.

claims.claim: Confidence values such as '92%', '98%', '95%' represent statistical precision.
claims.evidence: No mathematical probability formula was used to compute 92% or 98%.
claims.potential_problem: Converts qualitative engineering confidence into misleading pseudo-statistical percentages.
claims.required_correction: Replace numerical percentages in DECISION_LOG.md and reports with qualitative classifications: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW with explicit rationale.
